en: The Triplet on the Visible (Sanidassanattika) and the Couplets on the Taints and Things Subject to Taints (Āsavasāsavaduka).
Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, both a taint and associated with taints,

there arises a state that is neither demonstrable nor reactive, and neither a taint nor dissociated from taints, by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, both a taint and associated with taints,
there arises a state that is neither demonstrable nor reactive, neither a taint nor dissociated from taints, and not visible-with-resistance.

By way of root condition ... [as before] ... dependent on a non-visible-non-obstructive state that is both an outflow and subject to outflows, there arise non-visible-obstructive states that are neither outflows nor subject to outflows, by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. There are six in the case of root, three in the case of object ... [as before] ... six in the case of non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, which is both with taints and not itself a taint, there arises, by way of root-condition, a state that is neither demonstrable nor reactive and is neither without taints nor not without taints. Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive,
which is both with taints and not itself a taint, there arises [a state] that is neither non-demonstrable nor reactive and is neither without taints nor not without taints.

A state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, impinging, and both with taints and not itself a taint, there arise states that are neither non-demonstrable nor impinging, and are neither not-with-taints nor not-a-taint, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. In the case of the root [condition]...
Three ... [and so on] ... three in the case of non-disappearance.
